international.title: UK government borrowing rises less than forecast in surprise boost for chancellor John Healey
international.summary: UK economy defies City predictions and Iran war fallout, with gap between spending and income about £1bn lower than expected in October, at £17bn The UK government borrowed less than expected in October despite a rise in debt interest costs, in a boost for chancellor John Healey amid the pressure on Britain’s economy from the Middle East war. The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said public sector net borrowing – the difference between government spending and income – was £17bn in October, about £800m higher than the same month a year ago. City economists had forecast borrowing would increase to £18bn. Continue reading...
